name: United States

eSignLaw.name: ESIGN Act and state UETA
eSignLaw.citation: 15 U.S.C. 7001 et seq.; UETA as enacted by most states

levelNote: A simple electronic signature is valid for most contracts when the signer intends to sign and consents to doing business electronically.
ageNote: In Alabama and Nebraska the age is 19, and in Mississippi 21.

formRequirements.note: Wills are excluded from the ESIGN Act; a few states allow electronic wills under their own rules.
Adoption, divorce and other family-law documents are excluded from the ESIGN Act.
Deeds and many property documents need notarization or recording formalities beyond a simple signature.

notices: Electronic signature law that applies: ESIGN Act and state UETA. A simple electronic signature is valid for most contracts when the signer intends to sign and consents to doing business electronically.
You must be at least 18 years old to sign this agreement. In Alabama and Nebraska the age is 19, and in Mississippi 21.
If you are unsure whether this applies to you, ask for a paper alternative before signing.
limitationNote: Written-contract periods vary by state (California is four years, New York six); six is the longer common one.
